- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is positive (≥0.3) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; cap upward forecasts at 1–2% above recent 7-day average.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is weak but price is falling — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% to align with sentiment-driven volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage mean reversion; if sentiment turns negative after a peak, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating 0.1–0.3), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
